Consult Summary:
- Patient with known heart failure presents with 2 weeks of progressive exertional dyspnea, worse over the past few days, with new bilateral ankle swelling and a mild dry cough; clinician suspects heart-failure exacerbation and plans increased diuretic therapy, blood tests, and echocardiogram with 1-week review.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Progressive shortness of breath over the last couple of weeks, markedly worse in the last few days.
  - Now breathless on minimal exertion (walking to shops, around house); requires sitting to catch breath.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms slowly worsening for ~2 weeks; became “quite troublesome” in past few days.
  - Bilateral ankle swelling noted for the past few days.
  - Mild dry cough present, not severe.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Symptoms provoked by minimal exertion (walking); relieved by sitting to catch breath.
  - Reports increased urinary frequency “ever since the drugs” (patient attribute to diuretic).
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - No chest pain.
  - No palpitations.
  - No fever.
  - Appetite normal.
  - Urination increased (patient comment).
  - Feels a bit run-down but otherwise “pretty normal.”
- Pertinent negatives:
  - Denies chest pain, palpitations, fever.
  - No current alcohol use.
  - No current smoking (former smoker).

Past Medical History:
- Heart failure (previous diagnosis; episodes of ankle swelling during prior decompensation).
  - Medications related to heart condition explicitly mentioned: Furosemide (dose/route/frequency not documented), Bisoprolol (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Myocardial infarction described as a “small heart attack” approximately 5 years ago; required a short hospital stay.
- Other conditions: none reported.
- Allergies: None reported.

Medications (explicitly mentioned):
- Furosemide — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Aspirin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Bisoprolol — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Social History:
- Lives alone with two pet cats (names Polly and Tim).
- Occupation: part-time lorry driver; day shifts only; work can be exhausting.
- Smoking: Former smoker; approximately 1 pack per day for ~25 years; has stopped (timing of cessation not documented).
- Alcohol: Does not drink.
- Exercise: Walks to the shops about once daily; no vigorous exercise.

Family History:
- Father died of a heart attack in his early sixties.
- Mother alive with osteoporosis.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented as numeric values.
- Exam findings documented by clinician:
  - “Chest, saturations and blood pressure are all OK” per clinician after examining the patient (no numeric values provided).
  - Bilateral ankle swelling noted by patient (patient-reported; clinician acknowledged swelling).
- No other physical exam findings documented in transcript.

Investigations:
- No investigation results reported.
- Planned/ordered:
  - Blood tests: full blood count and renal function (clinician specified checking kidney function and looking for anemia).
  - Echocardiogram (cardiac ultrasound) requested; expected scheduling timeframe approximately 1–2 weeks.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected acute decompensation / flare-up of chronic heart failure (volume overload)
  - Assessment details:
    - Based on progressive exertional dyspnea, bilateral ankle swelling, history of heart failure, and clinician examination.
  - Plan items:
    - Increase Furosemide from current regimen to “one tablet twice a day” (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Arrange blood tests: full blood count and kidney function (renal panel) to assess safety and baseline.
    - Arrange echocardiogram to assess cardiac function (may take 1–2 weeks to organize).
    - Clinic follow-up in ~1 week to reassess symptoms and response to diuretic increase.
    - Safety-netting: patient instructed to contact clinician sooner if worsening breathlessness or new chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness.
- Issue 2: Bilateral ankle edema
  - Assessment details:
    - Likely secondary to fluid retention from heart-failure exacerbation.
  - Plan items:
    - Managed as part of diuretic adjustment (see Issue 1).
    - Monitor response and reassess at follow-up.
- Issue 3: Mild dry cough and fatigue / reduced exercise tolerance
  - Assessment details:
    - Symptoms contemporaneous with suspected heart-failure exacerbation; no alternative cause established in transcript.
  - Plan items:
    - Symptom monitoring; reassess at follow-up and after investigations.
- General plan items:
  - Medication reconciliation and review (explicit doses not documented; clinician to verify current medications and dosing).
  - Reinforce urgent contact if symptoms acutely worsen.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Numeric vital signs (blood pressure, heart rate, respiratory rate, temperature, oxygen saturation) not documented.
  - Weight and recent weight change not documented.
  - Exact doses, routes, and frequencies for current medications (Furosemide, Bisoprolol, Aspirin) not documented.
  - Results of any recent investigations (ECG, BNP, prior echocardiogram) not provided.
  - Physical exam details (heart and lung auscultation findings) not recorded.
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - None substantive. (There was brief clarifying exchange about which beta-blocker — clinician asked “Metoprolol?” and patient confirmed “Bisoprolol”; patient’s statement is taken as definitive.)
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Connection/intermittent audio issues noted by clinician at times; a few phrases were difficult to hear. Overall history was obtainable but some details (medication doses, exam specifics) were not provided.
